research.brief: Người đặt đồ ăn vặt và thức uống ở Việt Nam, chủ yếu thao tác trên điện thoại; có thể là khách vãng lai, khách đăng nhập hoặc nhân viên admin.

highlights.text: In PwC's 2025 Vietnam sample of 517 consumers, 58% bought prepared food at least weekly and 54% ordered takeaway to their home; the study does not describe Kat's own customers.
Decision Lab reported that 65% of eligible residents in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Da Nang had ordered from a food-delivery app in the past month, using 1.7 apps on average.

Decision Lab's 2025 market study identifies ShopeeFood and GrabFood as the two largest food-delivery alternatives in its surveyed market; this is a market signal, not a measure of Kat customer preferences.

Baymard's US e-commerce research reports extra costs and forced account creation among checkout friction points; its percentages are not Vietnam estimates, but the findings support clear fees and a visible guest path.

PwC's 2025 Vietnam survey says price remains a primary food-purchase driver, so showing item prices, delivery fees and voucher savings together may help people judge value; this is a design inference.

notes: Follow the patterns of the apps they live in before inventing new ones (practices.md sections 2 and 3).

market.gap: This short desk review did not identify a reliable unmet market need; validate any differentiation with Kat customers.
